correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact predator inequality v' >= -dv, substitutes the resulting lower bound into the prey equation, and applies the transformation w=u^(1-p) only while u is positive. The integrating-factor estimate is exact. If the resulting upper bound for w becomes negative at T, positivity through T is impossible, so a first prey-extinction time must occur before T. The closed-form k threshold follows from the monotonic bound Phi_k(s)<=Phi_k(T). The high-precision verifier reproduces all source-data numbers and confirms strict margins at k=16.

value.rationale: Finite-time fear-driven extinction is a headline biological and mathematical conclusion of the motivating article, and the source itself notes that quantitative control of the fear strength remains unresolved. The new result turns that qualitative mechanism into a finite-horizon, directly checkable condition and applies it to the source's own initial data. It also distinguishes a rigorously certified regime from the paper's much smaller simulation value instead of using numerics as proof. This is a substantive boundary/quantification result rather than a cosmetic correction.
